description.value: A local history museum housed in a restored 1908 'kit house' farmstead within the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve on Pender Island. The museum tells stories of the W̱SÁNEĆ People and settler families through artifacts including an ancient sandstone whale carving. The waterfront location features a heritage orchard with picnic tables and trail access to Ella Bay at low tide.

address.value: 2408 South Otter Bay Road, Pender Island, V0N 2M1

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The /visit/ subpage explicitly states 'Bike racks are also available there' near the turquoise cabin, confirming bike parking. The same page confirms washrooms: 'The turquoise cabin houses two modern, accessible washrooms.' The address on the website (2408 South Otter Bay Road, Pender Island, V0N 2M1) matches OSM exactly. The website lists phone (250) 629-6935 which OSM lacks. No evidence for water refill, Wi-Fi, charging, showers, food, or any other optional amenities.
concerns: OSM has no phone number; website lists (250) 629-6935 during open hours and 250.217.0823 for off-hours visits
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active community museum with bike racks and accessible washrooms, located within a national park reserve on a popular Gulf Islands cycling route. Clear fit for touring cyclists visiting Pender Island.
enrichment_extras.notes: Museum is seasonal; accessible by bike, boat, or kayak. Email: pendermuseum@shaw.ca

Bike parking.detail: Bike racks available beside the turquoise cabin opposite the museum

Washrooms.detail: Two modern, accessible washrooms in the turquoise cabin; no washrooms inside the museum itself

wow_evidence: Museum in a 1908 kit farmhouse within the national park reserve, with W̱SÁNEĆ stories and a heritage orchard.
blurb: Island museum in a 1908 farmhouse above Ella Bay, Pender Island.
